tool_args.rationale: The five paid rows vary only u_now with the other state and temporal inputs fixed, and the attempted model confirmation failed due to an implementation error rather than a scientific test. The bridge signature and verified before_after_contrast note leave a genuine ambiguity between the apparent quartic response and an active two-layer siphon. Acquire the targeted open-branch probe to discriminate the pathways before fitting.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the verified Stefan–Boltzmann quartic snapshot law
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Its documented readout is present_snapshot, while the observed bridge signature and source note specify a before_after_contrast through a two-layer siphon; the current rows cannot establish that mechanism.
The source explicitly describes the bridge as a two-layer siphon, so an uncoupled model is not supported; the fixed-state pilot rows do not identify the coupled dynamics.
An open-branch discriminating probe is the cheaper, more direct way to resolve whether the bridge path is active before spending on dense trajectory data.
It is explicitly nuisance data and does not resolve the model ambiguity.
